node-1.label: Patient currently has lethargy, delayed sleep, and uncomfortable sensations in arms that appear at night/during rest and are partially relieved by movement

node-2.label: Patient is a 48-year-old female with a 14-year history of auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions; medical history includes hypertension for 7 years, uterine fibroid disease for 3 years, and iron deficiency anaemia for many years

node-3.label: Patient was previously treated with olanzapine 20mg/day in 2019; current symptoms emerged after starting olanzapine and worsened with increased nighttime dosing

node-4.label: Physical examination on admission was unremarkable

why.why: Laboratory results show severe iron deficiency (ferritin 2.0 ng/mL, iron 2.0 μmol/L) and anemia (Hb 63 g/L), which directly support iron-deficiency-driven secondary restless legs syndrome. A therapeutic olanzapine level (53.5 ng/mL) with reported dose-related worsening further implicates medication as a contributing or exacerbating factor. Normal physical examination excludes focal neurological causes, and the characteristic nocturnal limb discomfort with movement relief fits secondary RLS. Confidence is therefore increased from 0.75 to 0.92.

New laboratory evidence of severe iron deficiency and anemia provides a more parsimonious organic explanation for the nocturnal sensory-motor symptoms, reducing the likelihood that this is primarily a drug-induced movement disorder. Although olanzapine exposure and therapeutic levels may contribute to or worsen symptoms, the characteristic night-time limb discomfort relieved by movement and the iron-deficiency state are more consistent with secondary RLS. Confidence is decreased from 0.3 to 0.2.

The presence of severe iron deficiency and anemia, along with characteristic nocturnal limb discomfort partially relieved by movement, indicates an organic sensorimotor disorder rather than a primary psychiatric sleep disturbance. The emergence and worsening of symptoms after olanzapine use also argues against primary psychiatric sleep disturbance. Confidence is decreased from 0.2 to 0.1.
